analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time. 我辞职了，因为我在那家公司已经不开心很久了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者自述 I resigned 的直接陈述。男士开口第一段就说 It's my last day at work tomorrow. I'll start my new job in two weeks.，到第三段又点明 I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time。『resigned』『last day』『new job』几个自述合起来，明确他要离开现职——这是说话人自己交代现状的直接信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I resigned ↔leave his present job resign 等于 leave the job It's my last day at work tomorrow. ↔leave his present job 明天最后一天即将离职

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了 tell them how I really feel 这串原词，但男士说的是 I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel（不确定该不该说），是犹豫，不是『他将会说』。把『不确定 要不要』听成『他会』，正中圈套。 借用原文：I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel B) 原词陷阱 选项偷用了 in two weeks 这个时间词，但原文是 I'll start my new job in two weeks（两 周后开始新工作），根本没提『见新经理』。听到 two weeks 就选 B，是被数字原词牵着 走。 借用原文：I'll start my new job in two weeks C) 偷换概念 选项借了原文反复出现的 interview 一词，但原文的 conduct an interview with me before I leave 和 an exit interview 是『离职面谈』，而非 a job interview（求职面 试）。同一个 interview，性质完全不同。 借用原文：an exit interview

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: it could affect 表担忧的因果句。男士说 Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose，紧接 There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry。could affect 点出他改主意的原因——怕影响声誉和 人脉；下一段女士又用 injuring your future career prospects 把这归结为『损害未来职业 前景』，因果信号明确。

analysis.text: A) 未提及 选项 negative impression on the interviewer 借了话题里的 interview 氛围，但男士担心 的是声誉和人脉、行业里的名声，从没提『给面试官留下负面印象』。这是没有依据的添 加。 C) 张冠李戴 选项盗用了第6段 dirt against another manager 的 manager 语境，但那是女士讲『信息 被用来对付别的经理』，并非男士改主意是怕惹自己的顶头上司。把别处的内容嫁接到本题 原因上，是张冠李戴。 借用原文：used as dirt against another manager D) 未提及 选项 harm to his fellow employees 在录音里找不到对应：男士担心的是自己的前途，女 士谈的是信息被高管滥用，谁都没说会伤到同事。这是凭空捏造的受害对象。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your- employer websites. 也许更好的办法是去那些给雇主打分的网站上把心里话一吐为快。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Perhaps it would be better 表打算的建议句。对话临近结尾，男士说 Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites。it would be better 直接表达他认为更好的做法，正是题干『had better do』 要找的打算句，出现在对话后半段，符合建议常落尾部的规律。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: getting things off my chest ↔Pour out his frustrations get off chest 等于 pour out frustrations going to one of those rate-your-employer websites ↔on a rate-your-employer website 同一渠道名几乎原样对应

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 选项 Prepare a comprehensive exit report 借了话题里的 exit 一词，造出『写一份详尽的 离职报告』，但录音里男士从没说要写报告。这是凭空添加的方案。 B) 原词陷阱 选项 Do some practice for the exit interview 盗用了 exit interview 这一原词，但全程没 有任何人提到『为面谈做练习』；女士最后反而说 don't do the interview at all（干脆别 做这面谈）。听到 exit interview 就选，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：don't do the interview at all C) 原词陷阱 选项 Network with his close friends to find a better employer 借了第7段 network in the industry 的 network 一词，但原文的 network 是『在行业建人脉』且是怕受损，并非 『找好友另找雇主』。盗 network 来拼错意，是原词陷阱。 借用原文：my ability to network in the industry 1 M: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Forster. M: 今天，我将与著名植物学家 Jane Forster 交谈。 2 W: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry. W: 感谢你邀请我来参加节目，Henry。 3 M: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it? M: 最近，Jane，自从你最新的纪录片发布以来，你已经成为了名人。你能跟我们讲讲这部片子吗？ 4 W: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia. W: 嗯，它记录了我去研究东南亚赤道地区雨林原生植被的探险。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 M: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations. M: 你确实去了一些非常exotic的地方。 6 W: It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream. W: 说实话，那一点都不glamorous。我们去的地区只能乘独木舟到达，小屋里的生活条件简陋至极。没 有电，我们的水源是附近的一条小溪。 7 M: How were the weather conditions while you were there? M: 你们在那里时天气状况如何？ 8 W: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable. At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing. It was too humid to either work or sleep. W: 天气对我们的工作完全不利，因为湿度几乎让人无法忍受。中午的时候，我们就待在小屋里什么都不 做。太潮湿了，既没法工作也没法睡觉。 9 M: How long did your team spend in the jungle? M: 你的团队在丛林里待了多久？ 10 W: Originally, we planned to be there for a month. But in the end, we stayed for only two weeks. W: 原本，我们计划在那里待一个月。但最后，我们只待了两周。 11 M: Why did you cut the expedition short? M: 你们为什么提前结束探险？ 12 W: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice. W: 行程进行到一半时，我们收到消息说有飓风正在接近。我们不得不非常仓促地撤离。 13 M: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote. M: 听起来像是个引人入胜的故事。 14 W: It was frightening. The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids. We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment. W: 很吓人的。最快的撤离路线是穿过急流。我们不得不带着所有设备穿越那些急流。 15 M: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful? M: 那么总的来说，这次旅程是不成功的吗？ 16 W: Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life. W: 绝对不是。我们收集了大量关于当地植物的数据。 17 M: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions? M: 你为什么要忍受这样恶劣的条件？ 18 W: Botany is an obsession for me. Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery. And I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world. W: 植物学对我来说是一种痴迷。我去的很多地方都有令人惊叹的风景。而且我能遇到来自世界各地的各 种各样的人。 19 M: So where will your next destination be? M: 那你下一个目的地会是哪里？ 20 W: I haven't decided yet. W: 我还没决定。 21 M: Then we can leave it for another occasion. Thanks. M: 那我们可以留待下次再聊。谢谢。

B) 原词陷阱 month-long expedition 借了她回答里 my expedition 与 planned to be there for a month 的原词拼成，但主持人开场请她谈的是纪录片本身，不是"为期一月的远征"这件事， 属答非所问。 借用原文：my expedition D) 原词陷阱 career as a botanist 借了开场 the renowned botanist 的原词，但主持人没有请她谈"植 物学家的职业生涯"，只请她谈纪录片，听到 botanist 就选属答非所问。 借用原文：the renowned botanist

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream. 老实说，那远谈不上光鲜。我们去的地方只能靠独木舟进入，小屋里的居住条件说轻点也是 非常原始的。没有电。我们的水源就是附近一条小溪。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 原话之后的连串列举。信号是她说完 far from glamorous 后一口气列举多重恶劣条件： accessible only by canoe、living conditions in the hut were primitive、no electricity、water supply was a nearby stream。连珠炮式的多项困难，正是答案句。

questions.stem: What does the woman think of the journey?
questions.stemZh: 女士如何看待这次旅程?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life. 绝对不是。我们采集了关于当地植物的海量数据。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 强烈否定 + 反转后的正向定调。信号是主持人问 was the journey unsuccessful?（负面设 问），她以 Absolutely not. 强烈否定反转，再用 gathered a massive amount of data 给 出正向定调——"不是失败、收获巨大"才是她的真实态度。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: We gathered a massive amount of data ↔It was fruitful. 采集海量数据等于有收获

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 memorable（难忘）听上去是正面评价，像能套上整段经历，但她对行程的总评落点是"有 收获"，原文并未说"难忘"，属凭褒义氛围误推、原文未提及的态度。 B) 与原文相反 unbearable 盗自 the humidity was almost unbearable，那是形容潮湿天气难忍，并非 她对整段 journey 的评价；况且她明确否定行程失败，态度是正面，与 unbearable 相反。 借用原文：the humidity was almost unbearable C) 与原文相反 uneventful（平淡无事）与原文截然相反——她经历了飓风逼近、紧急撤离、激流行船，行 程绝非平淡，这是把惊险经历反说成平淡的反向干扰。 借用原文：It was frightening. Section B 1 Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen. Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice. In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms. They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics. It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text. Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained. 科学家在与外行交流时经常使用专业术语。他们中的大多数人没有意识到这种做法的有害影响。在一项新 研究中,人们在阅读关于自动驾驶车辆和手术机器人等主题时接触到专业术语后表示,他们对科学的兴趣不 如那些阅读相同主题但没有使用专业术语的人。他们也感觉自己对科学了解较少,不太有资格讨论科学话 题。值得注意的是,即使文中对专业术语进行了定义也没有作用。即使术语被定义了,读者仍然感受到与阅 读未被解释的专业术语时相同的参与感缺失。 2 The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers. Hillary Schulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal. They are often emulating bad managers they've had in the past. It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course. They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style. 大多数人不喜欢自己的工作。这是一个令人惊讶但却是统计事实。根据最新研究,员工不满的一个主要原因 是,许多人认为他们的管理者很糟糕。不过,很少有人将他们的管理者描述为恶意或善于操纵的。虽然这类 人确实存在,但他们是少数。看起来,大多数管理者只是不知道更好的做法。他们往往在效仿过去遇到的糟 糕管理者。他们很可能从未读过管理书籍或参加过管理课程。他们甚至可能从未思考过什么是好的管理,以 及这会如何影响他们自己的管理风格。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 2 The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had. From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs. 研究人员就员工的管理者对他们进行了访谈,首先询问他们遇到过的最糟糕的管理者。由此,研究人员总结 出了为什么有些管理者被认为工作做得非常糟糕的四个主要原因。 3 The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Often a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic. 第一个原因是公司文化,员工认为这助长了糟糕的管理做法。具体来说,压力大的工作环境、培训不足以及 缺乏问责制被认为是最应受到指责的。当管理者的上级未能对其不当行为进行惩处时,往往会有效地助长管 理者令人反感的行为。这样的工作场所有时被描述为有毒的。 4 The second cause was attributed to the managers' characteristics. Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people—those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general. 第二个原因归因于管理者的特征。那些被认为最具破坏性的是古怪的人——那些缺乏动力的人、那些将个 人问题带入工作场所的人,以及那些总体上性情或性格令人不快的人。 5 The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments. 糟糕管理的第三个原因与资质不足有关,这里说的不太是从大学获得的那种正式资质,而是来自可靠的工作 经验和职业成就的非正式资质。 6 The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential. One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest. It wasn't their skill set or other merits that got them the job; it was their tenure. 第四个原因涉及因潜力以外的原因而被提拔的管理者。这些人被提拔的一个特别原因是他们在职时间最 长。让他们获得这份工作的不是他们的技能或其他优点,而是他们的任期。 7 A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers. It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager. 值得指出的一点是,这项研究仅基于员工的视角。研究人员没有询问高层领导对一线管理者的看法。很有可 能他们对自己提拔的人现在的表现感到满意,对他们实际造成的损害毫不知情,这或许可以解释为什么,正如 研究人员总结的那样,这些中层管理者通常意识不到自己是糟糕的管理者。

matching.raw:
A) A hundred years before iconic figures like Bill Gates and Steve Jobs permeated our lives, an Irish- Italian inventor laid the foundation of the communication explosion of the 21st century. Guglielmo Marconi was arguably the first truly global figure in modern communication. Not only was he the first to communicate globally, he was the first to think globally about communication. Marconi may not have been the greatest inventor of his time, but more than anyone else, he brought about a fundamental shift in the way we communicate.
B) Today's globally networked media and communication system has its origins in the 19th century, when, for the first time, messages were sent electronically across great distances. The telegraph, the telephone, and radio were the obvious predecessors of the Internet, iPods, and mobile phones. What made the link from then to now was the development of wireless communication. Marconi was the first to develop and perfect this system, using the recently-discovered "air waves" that make up the electromagnetic spectrum.
C) Between 1896, when he applied for his first patent in England at the age of 22, and his death in Italy in 1937, Marconi was at the center of every major innovation in electronic communication. He was also a skilled and sophisticated organizer, an entrepreneurial innovator, who mastered the use of corporate strategy, media relations, government lobbying, international diplomacy, patents, and prosecution. Marconi was really interested in only one thing: the extension of mobile, personal, long- distance communication to the ends of the earth (and beyond, if we can believe some reports). Some like to refer to him as a genius, but if there was any genius to Marconi it was this vision.
D) In 1901 he succeeded in signaling across the Atlantic, from the west coast of England to Newfoundland in the USA, despite the claims of science that it could not be done. In 1924 he convinced the British government to encircle the world with a chain of wireless stations using the latest technology that he had devised, shortwave radio. There are some who say Marconi lost his edge when commercial broadcasting came along; he didn't see that radio could or should be used to frivolous(无聊的) ends. In one of his last public speeches, a radio broadcast to the United States in March 1937, he deplored that broadcasting had become a one-way means of communication and foresaw it moving in another direction, toward communication as a means of exchange. That was visionary genius.
E) Marconi's career was devoted to making wireless communication happen cheaply, efficiently, smoothly, and with an elegance that would appear to be intuitive and uncomplicated to the user- friendly, if you will. There is a direct connection from Marconi to today's social media, search engines, and program streaming that can best be summed up by an admittedly provocative exclamation: the 20th century did not exist. In a sense, Marconi's vision jumped from his time to our own.
F) Marconi invented the idea of global communication—or, more straightforwardly, globally networked, mobile, wireless communication. Initially, this was wireless Morse code telegraphy(电报通讯), the principal communication technology of his day. Marconi was the first to develop a practical method for wireless telegraphy using radio waves. He borrowed technical details from many sources, but what set him apart was a self-confident vision of the power of communication technology on the one hand, and, on the other, of the steps that needed to be taken to consolidate his own position as a player in that field. Tracing Marconi's lifeline leads us into the story of modern communication itself. There were other important figures, but Marconi towered over them all in reach, power, and influence, as well as in the grip he had on the popular imagination of his time. Marconi was quite simply the central figure in the emergence of a modern understanding of communication.
G) In his lifetime, Marconi foresaw the development of television and the fax machine, GPS, radar, and the portable hand-held telephone. Two months before he died, newspapers were reporting that he was working on a "death ray," and that he had "killed a rat with an intricate device at a distance of three feet." By then, anything Marconi said or did was newsworthy. Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements. If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.
H) Marconi's biography is also a story about choices and the motivations behind them. At one level, Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class. On another scale, he was a perpetual outsider. Wherever he went, he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," considered foreign in Britain, British in Italy, and "not American" in the United States. At the same time, he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance that drove, and sometimes stained, every one of his relationships.
I) Marconi placed a permanent stamp on the way we live. He was the first person to imagine a practical application for the wireless spectrum, and to develop it successfully into a global communication system—in both terms of the word; that is, worldwide and all-inclusive. He was able to do this because of a combination of factors—most important, timing and opportunity—but the single- mindedness and determination with which he carried out his self-imposed mission was fundamentally character-based; millions of Marconi's contemporaries had the same class, gender, race, and colonial privilege as he, but only a handful did anything with it. Marconi needed to achieve the goal that was set in his mind as an adolescent; by the time he reached adulthood, he understood, intuitively, that in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power. Disciplined, uncritical loyalty to political power became his compass for the choices he had to make.
J) At the same time, Marconi was uncompromisingly independent intellectually. Shortly after Marconi's death, the nuclear physicist Enrico Fermi—soon to be the developer of the Manhattan Project—wrote that Marconi proved that theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress. "Experience can rarely, unless guided by a theoretical concept, arrive at results of any great significance…on the other hand, an excessive trust in theoretical conviction would have prevented Marconi from persisting in experiments which were destined to bring about a revolution in the technique of radio-communications." In other words, Marconi had the advantage of not being burdened by preconceived assumptions.
K) The most controversial aspect of Marconi's life—and the reason why there has been no satisfying biography of Marconi until now—was his uncritical embrace of Benito Mussolini. At first this was not problematic for him. But as the regressive(倒退的) nature of Mussolini's regime became clear, he began to suffer a crisis of conscience. However, after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully (as president of Italy's national research council and royal academy, as well as a member of the Fascist Grand Council) until the day he died—conveniently—in 1937, shortly before he would have had to take a stand in the conflict that consumed a world that he had, in part, created. 36. Marconi was central to our present-day understanding of communication.

Two months before he died, newspapers were reporting that he was working on a "death ray," and that he had "killed a rat with an intricate device at a distance of three feet." By then, anything Marconi said or did was newsworthy. Stock prices rose or sank according to his pronouncements. If Marconi said he thought it might rain, there was likely to be a run on umbrellas.

blocks.label: H
blocks.text: Marconi's biography is also a story about choices and the motivations behind them. At one level, Marconi could be fiercely autonomous and independent of the constraints of his own social class. On another scale, he was a perpetual outsider. Wherever he went, he was never "of" the group; he was always the "other," considered foreign in Britain, British in Italy, and "not American" in the United States. At the same time, he also suffered tremendously from a need for acceptance that drove, and sometimes stained, every one of his relationships.

blocks.label: I
blocks.text: Marconi placed a permanent stamp on the way we live. He was the first person to imagine a practical application for the wireless spectrum, and to develop it successfully into a global communication system—in both terms of the word; that is, worldwide and all-inclusive. He was able to do this because of a combination of factors—most important, timing and opportunity—but the single- mindedness and determination with which he carried out his self-imposed mission was fundamentally character-based; millions of Marconi's contemporaries had the same class, gender, race, and colonial privilege as he, but only a handful did anything with it. Marconi needed to achieve the goal that was set in his mind as an adolescent; by the time he reached adulthood, he understood, intuitively, that in order to have an impact he had to both develop an independent economic base and align himself with political power. Disciplined, uncritical loyalty to political power became his compass for the choices he had to make.

blocks.label: J
blocks.text: At the same time, Marconi was uncompromisingly independent intellectually. Shortly after Marconi's death, the nuclear physicist Enrico Fermi—soon to be the developer of the Manhattan Project—wrote that Marconi proved that theory and experimentation were complementary features of progress. "Experience can rarely, unless guided by a theoretical concept, arrive at results of any great significance…on the other hand, an excessive trust in theoretical conviction would have prevented Marconi from persisting in experiments which were destined to bring about a revolution in the technique of radio-communications." In other words, Marconi had the advantage of not being burdened by preconceived assumptions.

blocks.label: K
blocks.text: The most controversial aspect of Marconi's life—and the reason why there has been no satisfying biography of Marconi until now—was his uncritical embrace of Benito Mussolini. At first this was not problematic for him. But as the regressive(倒退的) nature of Mussolini's regime became clear, he began to suffer a crisis of conscience. However, after a lifetime of moving within the circles of power, he was unable to break with authority, and served Mussolini faithfully (as president of Italy's national research council and royal academy, as well as a member of the Fascist Grand Council) until the day he died—conveniently—in 1937, shortly before he would have had to take a stand in the conflict that consumed a world that he had, in part, created. 36. Marconi was central to our present-day understanding of communication.

P1 Humans are fascinated by the source of their failings and virtues: This preoccupation inevitably leads to an old debate: whether nature or nurture moulds us more. A revolution in genetics has poised this as a modern political question about the character of our society: if personalities are hard-wired into our genes, what can governments do to help us? It feels morally questionable, yet claims of genetic selection by intelligence are making headlines.

P2 This is down to "hereditarian"(遗传论的) science and a recent paper claimed "differences in exam performance between pupils attending selective and non-selective schools mirror the genetic differences between them". With such an assertion, the work was predictably greeted by a lot of absurd claims about "genetics determining academic success". What the research revealed was the rather less surprising result: the educational benefits of selective schools largely disappear once pupils' inborn ability and socio-economic background were taken into account. It is a glimpse of the blindingly obvious—and there's nothing to back strongly either a hereditary or environmental argument. 

P3 Yet the paper does say children are "unintentionally genetically selected" by the school system. Central to hereditarian science is a tall claim: that identifiable variations in genetic sequences can predict an individual's aptness to learn, reason and solve problems. This is problematic on many levels. A teacher could not seriously tell a parent their child has a low genetic tendency to study when external factors clearly exist. Unlike-minded academics say the inheritability of human traits is scientifically unsound. At best there is a weak statistical association and not a causal link between DNA and intelligence. Yet sophisticated statistics are used to create an intimidatory atmosphere of scientific certainty.

P4 While there's an undoubted genetic basis to individual difference, it is wrong to think that socially defined groups can be genetically accounted for. The fixation on genes as destiny is surely false too. Medical predictability can rarely be based on DNA alone; the environment matters too. Something as complex as intellect is likely to be affected by many factors beyond genes. If hereditarians want to advance their cause it will require more balanced interpretation and not just acts of advocacy.

P5 Genetic selection is a way of exerting influence over others, "the ultimate collective control of human destinies," as writer H. G. Wells put it. Knowledge becomes power and power requires a sense of responsibility. In understanding cognitive ability, we must not elevate discrimination to a science, allowing people to climb the ladder of life only as far as their cells might suggest. This will need a more sceptical eye on the science. As technology progresses, we all have a duty to make sure that we shape a future that we would want to find ourselves in.

P1 Nicola Sturgeon's speech last Tuesday setting out the Scottish government's legislative programme for the year ahead confirmed what was already pretty clear. Scottish councils are set to be the first in the UK with the power to levy charges on visitors, with Edinburgh likely to lead the way.

P2 Tourist taxes are not new. The Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan has a longstanding policy of charging visitors a daily fee. France's tax on overnight stays was introduced to assist thermal spa(温泉) towns to develop, and around half of French local authorities use it today.

P3 But such levies are on the rise. Moves by Barcelona and Venice to deal with the phenomenon of "over-tourism" through the use of charges have recently gained prominence. Japan and Greece are among the countries to have recently introduced tourist taxes.

P4 That the UK lags behind is due to our weak, by international standards, local government, as well as the opposition to taxes and regulation of our aggressively pro-market ruling party. Some UK cities have lobbied without success for the power to levy a charge on visitors. Such levies are no universal remedy as the amounts raised would be tiny compared with what has been taken away by central government since 2010. Still, it is to be hoped that the Scottish government's bold move will prompt others to act. There is no reason why visitors to the UK, or domestic tourists on holiday in hotspots such as Cornwall, should be exempt from taxation-particularly when vital local services including waste collection, park maintenance and arts and culture spending are under unprecedented strain.

P5 On the contrary, compelling tourists to make a financial contribution to the places they visit beyond their personal consumption should be part of a wider cultural shift. Westerners with disposable incomes have often behaved as if they have a right to go wherever they choose with little regard for the consequences. Just as the environmental harm caused by aviation and other transport must come under far greater scrutiny, the social cost of tourism must also be confronted. This includes the impact of short- term lets on housing costs and quality of life for residents. Several European capitals, including Paris and Berlin, are leading a campaign for tougher regulation by the European Union. It also includes the impact of overcrowding, litter and the kinds of behaviour associated with noisy parties.

P6 There is no "one size fits all" solution to this problem. The existence of new revenue streams for some but not all councils is complicated, and businesses are often opposed, fearing higher costs will make them uncompetitive. But those places that want them must be given the chance to make tourist taxes work. 51. What do we learn from Nicola Sturgeon's speech? A) The UK is set to adjust its policy on taxation. B) Tourists will have to pay a tax to visit Scotland. C) The UK will take new measures to boost tourism. D) Edinburgh contributes most to Scotland's tourism.

writing.model: As is vividly shown in the line graph above, the degree of urbanization in China rose steadily and remarkably over nearly four decades. Specifically, the proportion of urban population climbed from a mere 19.39% in 1980 to a striking 60.6% in 2019, tripling within the period, with the growth becoming especially rapid after the year 2000. Behind this rapid urbanization lie China's tremendous achievements. To begin with, decades of sustained economic growth created vast job opportunities in cities, drawing hundreds of millions of rural residents into urban areas. Moreover, forward-looking government policies and large-scale infrastructure construction accelerated the transfer of population and industries from the countryside to towns. Such progress not only reflects the modernization of the nation but also greatly improves people's living standards and promotes balanced regional development. In conclusion, the impressive climb of the urbanization curve mirrors the remarkable strides China has made. If this momentum is sustained wisely, the country will surely embrace an even brighter and more prosperous future.

sentences.text: 建省以来作时间状语 + 两句衔接 1988年建省以来 译成 Since it was established as a province in 1988，作句首时间状语，并触 发现在完成时。三大产业用并列名词作主语共一个谓语 have developed rapidly。第二层 是中国 唯一的省级经济特区 主语换成 Hainan/it，单独成句 It is also China's only provincial-level special economic zone，用 also 与前句衔接、点明它的特殊身份。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 偏离全篇基调：「建省以来飞速发展」是从 1988 持续至今，用现在完成时 have developed； 「是经济特区」是当前事实，回到一般现在时 is。 主谓一致 主语是三个产业并列（tourism, the service industry and the high-tech industry），是复数概 念 谓语用 have developed，不是 has。 语态 「建省」对海南是被动（海南被设立为省），译 it was established as a province，用被动。 冠词 the service industry、the high-tech industry 特指这两个行业加 the；China's only... 用所有格 + only 表「唯一」。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Since it was established as a province in 1988, Hainan's tourism, service industry and high-tech industry have developed rapidly, making it China's only provincial- level special economic zone. 4. 在中央政府和全国人民的大力支持下，海南将建成中国最大的自由贸易试验区。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 海南将被建成自由贸易试验区（主语策略：转被动） 中文 海南将建成中国最大的自由贸易试验区 形式上海南是主语，但「建成」的动作是别人对海南 做的，海南是被建设的对象。骨架取被动：Hainan will be built into China's largest free trade pilot zone，主语 Hainan、谓语 will be built（被动 + 将来）、into 引出结果。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「在…支持下」降级为介词短语 在中央政府和全国人民的大力支持下 是个「在…下」的状语，不是主干，降级成介词短语 With the strong support of the central government and people across the country，放在句首作 伴随/条件状语，逗号隔开。主干保持 Hainan will be built into...。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 偏离全篇基调：「将建成」是未来规划，用一般将来时 will be built。 语态 「建成」承受者是海南，用被动 will be built into，主体考生易误写主动 will build。 最高级与冠词 「最大的」用最高级 largest，前面 China's 所有格已限定，故说 China's largest free trade pilot zone（所有格后不再加 the）。 搭配 「建成…」用 be built into（建成为某物），介词用 into；「大力支持」strong support，「全国 人民」people across the country / nationwide。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the strong support of the central government and people across the country, Hainan will be built into the largest free trade pilot zone in China. 英语六级 2021年6月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
